title: Best Business Card Designers (2026): How to Hire One
h1: Best Business Card and Stationery Designers
description: How to hire a business card or stationery designer: what the package should include, print-ready files, price factors and red flags.
intro: Business cards, letterheads and envelopes carry your brand into meetings and letters. They are small jobs, but small mistakes, such as a wrong phone number or missing bleed, are expensive once printed. Stationery goes wrong when details are not proofread, the file does not match the printer's template, or text is too small to read. This guide helps you get it right the first time.

faq.q: What size should my business card be?
faq.a: Standard sizes differ by country, for example 85 by 55 millimeters in much of Europe and 3.5 by 2 inches in the US. Ask your printer and tell the designer.

faq.q: Do I need a logo first?
faq.a: It helps. A business card is usually built around your logo and brand colors. If you have none, consider ordering a logo first.

faq.q: Which files does the printer need?
faq.a: Usually a print-ready PDF with bleed and the right color settings. Ask your printer for their exact requirements.

faq.q: Should I add a QR code?
faq.a: It can be useful, linking to your website or contact details. Test it with several phones before printing.
Letterheads, envelopes, compliment slips, invoices and email signatures. Ordering them together keeps the look consistent.
